name: Action Against Hunger USA
mission: Action Against Hunger’s mission is to save the lives of children and their families. We are there for them before and after disaster strikes. We enable people to provide for themselves, see their children grow up strong, and for whole communities to prosper. We constantly search for more effective solutions, while sharing our knowledge and expertise with the world. We push for long-term change.
theoryOfChange: Hunger is predictable, preventable, and treatable.

strengths_deep_dive: Action Against Hunger USA combines lean administrative spending with widespread operational reach. By directing <cite id="15">90.4% of spending into field programs</cite> in FY2024, the charity ensures minimal leakage to overhead [15]. Its robust financial position includes <cite id="15">10.2 months of working capital</cite>, giving the organization stability despite a 20% revenue drop between FY2023 and FY2024 [2, 3, 15]. Third-party rating systems reflect these practices, awarding the organization an <cite id="15">89/100 overall score on Charity Navigator</cite> alongside <cite id="15">full compliance with all 20 BBB Wise Giving Alliance standards</cite> [15].
rich_narrative.summary: Action Against Hunger USA delivers high-impact global health and nutrition programs, operating as a primary humanitarian responder in high-need crisis zones [12]. In FY2024, the charity generated <cite id="3">$160,756,238 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting a recent contraction from $201,188,874 in FY2023 [2, 3]. Despite this annual drop in funding, the organization maintained exceptional financial efficiency, allocating <cite id="15">90.4% of its expenses directly to programs</cite> [15]. This significantly exceeds the <cite id="15">75% sector benchmark</cite> and the <cite id="15">83.5% peer median</cite> [15]. The organization holds an <cite id="15">89/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and earns Candid's highest Candid Seal [15]. Cost efficiency remains a core operational strength, with programming delivered at <cite id="14">$5.46 per beneficiary</cite> across direct nutrition, emergency response, and safe water initiatives [14].
